name: Peng Yongdong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Peng Yongdong is a director of KE Holdings, a real estate group focused on home sales and home rentals.
KE operates Lianjia, one of the world's largest real estate brokerages.
Peng was a senior consultant at IBM between 2006 and 2010 before joining KE.
Peng obtained his bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Zhejiang University in 2001 and an IMBA degree from Tsinghua University in 2006.

name: Tang Ye
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026); Hurun China U40 (2019-2021)
forbes_bio: Tang Ye chairs Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology, a supplier of laser-related software and hardware.
Friendess went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
Tang holds a master's degree in engineering management from China's prestigious Shanghai Jiaotong University.

name: Kuan Kam Hon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2016-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2022)
forbes_bio: Kuan Kam Hon was a high school dropout who began his career in construction in 1969. He worked at his father's company building high-end homes.
He set off on his own in 1978 and started Timol Weaving, a manufacturing business that made woven labels and badges.
Founded in 1988, his Hartalega Holdings is one of the world's largest makers of nitrile gloves with an annual production capacity of 40 billion gloves.
After more than doubling in 2020, shares of Hartalega fell in 2021 and 2022 due to a slump in demand for rubber gloves.
He is now a mentor and spokesman, leaving operations to his two sons. He shares his wealth with his brother Kuan Kam Peng.
forbes_facts: As the AIDS epidemic hit, Kam Hon moved into rubber and then synthetic gloves for the medical industry.
In 2005 Hartalega developed the world's first lightweight nitrile glove.

name: William Fung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: William Fung and his older brother Victor own a significant stake in Li & Fung, which operates as a middleman between global manufacturers and retailers in the U.S. and Europe.
William stepped down as chairman of Li & Fung in 2020 when Victor's son, Spencer, took the helm.
In 2020 Li & Fung was privatized through a deal worth $930 million.
In 2022, Danish shipping giant A.P. Moller-Maersk acquired the brothers' logistics business, LF Logistics, for $3.4 billion.
Their grandfather, Fung Pak-liu, founded Li & Fung with partner Li To-ming in 1906, exporting porcelain and silk.

name: Louis Bacon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: One of Wall Street's macro-trading legends, Louis Bacon cut his teeth as a commodities and currencies trader, earning big profits in the 1987 crash.
He created hedge fund Moore Capital in 1989 using trading profits and a small inheritance.
Bacon announced he was closing his hedge fund and returning outside investors' money in November 2019, citing years of "disappointing results."
Moore Capital still manages internal money and scored 70% returns in 2020 for Bacon and his employees.
forbes_facts: Bacon's environmental preservation-focused Moore Charitable Trust was defrauded out of $25 million by jailed banker Andy Caspersen.

name: Sebastian Siemiatkowski
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2025)
forbes_bio: Siemiatkowski cofounded Klarna in 2005, pioneering the buy-now, pay-later model in fintech. The firm lets consumers pay for small and large retail items in installments.
Klarna went public in September 2025 on the New York Stock Exchange at a $15 billion valuation; Siemiatkowski owns a 7% stake.
Klarna was valued by private investors at $45.6 billion in 2021, but the company's valuation was marked down significantly to $6.7 billion for its next funding round in 2022.
Siemiatkowski attended the Stockholm School of Economics and worked at an accounts-receivable factoring firm before starting Klarna.
Klarna is a fully licensed bank in Europe, where it offers checking accounts, savings accounts and debit cards.
Investors in Klarna include Sequoia Capital, BlackRock, Silver Lake, Bestseller Group and Ant Group.
forbes_facts: He met one of his Klarna cofounders while the two were flipping burgers at a Burger King in Sweden.

name: Wang Jinhua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Junmin chairs China Kings Resources, which sells fluorite products and develops fluorite mines.
Wang is a member of China's Communist Party.
China Kings is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.

name: Matthew Calkins
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2019-2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Matthew Calkins is the cofounder and CEO of Appian, a software development service with over $300 million in revenue.
Calkins cofounded the Reston, Virginia-based cloud computing company when he was 26. It went public on Nasdaq in May 2017.
Nearly one third of Appian's 350 customers are on the Forbes Global list of the world's biggest companies.
Calkins is also a board game player and designer who has won at the World Boardgaming Championships.
forbes_facts: A game theory whiz, Calkins wrote a thesis at Dartmouth explaining when a losing hockey team should pull its goalie.
